chart.title: The production of black tea

text: The diagram illustrates the stages involved in producing black tea, from picking the leaves to packing the finished product.

Overall, there are eight stages in the process, which begins on the tea plantation and ends with packing. Most of the stages change the leaves through drying and processing, and the tea is finally sold in two forms, as loose tea and in tea bags.

First, the top two leaves and the bud of each tea plant are picked by hand. The leaves are then spread on racks, where they are left to wither for 12 to 18 hours, after which they are rolled by machine. Next, they are left to oxidise for one to three hours, during which time they turn brown.

After oxidation, the leaves are dried in hot air at 120°C and then sorted according to size. At the following stage, the tea is tasted and graded. Finally, it is packed: larger leaves are sold as loose tea, whereas smaller pieces are used to fill tea bags, which completes the process.
